definition: Methods for estimating and expressing how confident or uncertain a model is about its predictions, beyond a single point estimate.
details: Uncertainty quantification is valuable for high-stakes applications, helping systems know when to defer to a human, request more information, or flag a response as potentially unreliable.
story: Picture a scoreboard at a science fair: you need a fair, agreed way to tell who actually won. A fair scoreboard keeps everyone honest. Before trusting a machine, someone has to measure how good it really is — fairly and honestly. A good metric is a ruler that does not bend when you lean on it. And that, done honestly, is Uncertainty Quantification.
